fixture.native_oracle: Four nonempty groups p0..p3, label+time exact and float rel 1e-11 absolute 1e-8

protocol: Two separate GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runners, one fixed row order, one offset by (batch*997)%4096 each batch. Each runner has 4 fresh server phase A0 large 1MiB/B1 small 32KiB/B2 small/A3 large, same exact 49152 logical rows and original RAW UUID TimeSeries v11 inner layout. STOP MERGES on TAGS,TimeRanges,SAMPLES for physical row accounting; QueryFinish INSERT/profile and process watchdog+worker CPU and write_bytes (separate and not interchangeable); global system.events worker-inclusive TAGS cache hits/misses; native full PromQL 3 warmup+6 measured each phase. Require no errors, actual TAGS physical row counts match global misses, same stable ID cardinality and exact independent oracle; A/A CPU/native wall <=25%.
math_bound: Nominal capacity of one cache entry =144 bytes. 1MiB cache admits 4096 unique repeated IDs. 32KiB holds only ~227; despite 4096 stable logical identities and 49152 sample references, small cache caused 46655 actual physical TAGS row writes (misses) instead of 4096, factor11.390381. Native read_rows rose 102400→144959, difference42559 EXACTLY equals extra physical TAGS rows 46655-4096, indicating each duplicate TAGS row was physically scanned in this fixture. Read bytes rose 5972069→10824906 (additional 4852837). CPU/wall speedups are end-to-end lab observations, not predicted directly by nominal entry counts.
confirmed: Both source/order jobs independently reproduce identical global cache hits and misses per capacity and physical TAGS row counts.
Full native labels/timestamps/numeric values same despite drastically different physical TAGS layout.
Small cache increases TAGS compressed physical bytes ~11.4x and server process write bytes 1.64-1.66x.
Within each runner, large-cache A/A native p50 wall drift <9% and process CPU drift <7%; small cache read wall p50 ratio 2.315/3.141 and query-log native CPU p50 ratio ~3.19/4.26.
Per-query QueryFinish INSERT CPU showed near-equal ~95ms despite increased whole-process CPU ~28-36%; this is instrumentation attribution caveat, not evidence of equal overall CPU.
negative_or_inconclusive: Fixed versus rotated row-order different native p50 ratios across TWO different machines, not a controlled within-runner order effect. Global cache hit/miss and total physical TAGS rows were exactly equal across both orders, so no observed capacity-cache hit-rate order effect for this fixture.
Real production default cache is100MiB, not32KiB; its relative working set, churn and hit rate are not known. Do not claim 100MiB inadequate or recommend global increase.

Merges stopped intentionally to capture raw ReplacingMergeTree duplicates; natural merging and sustained writes may change TAGS physical accumulation and query CPU. This is not a steady-state production performance claim.

method_failures.reason: Pipeline cache ProfileEvents absent from INSERT QueryFinish; physical baseline remained valid.
Fresh system.events cache keys omitted until first nonzero increments; required zero default instead of presence in start snapshot.

next_action.step: Run controlled same-runner small-cache fixed/rotate/rotate/fixed ABBA with same binary and original sorted fixture; require exact native oracle, worker-global hit/miss, physical TAGS/ID/sample checks and <=25% A/A CPU/wall drift. Separately test a cache-reset and natural-merges workload before any operational recommendation.
next_action.stop_condition: Never attribute between-runner read latency differences to input order; do not promote 100MiB cache change without actual production working set/PSI/RSS and sustained write/merge/reads.
